_comment: OUTPOST configuration. 'default' applies to every dataset; per-dataset blocks override it. These are the exact values behind every number in README.md. sim_topk_frac (SimSample) is ON for yelp only - on graphs whose degree is below the sampling budget it cannot select neighbours and instead removes edge subsampling, which is harmful (see analysis/FINDINGS.md).
_comment_demo: demo_default holds the DEMO baseline's own hyperparameters (--method demo merges default + demo_default + the dataset's input_dim and eval_batch_mult). mixup=True is DEMO's PUBLISHED configuration: their released main.py defaults it to False, which reproduces the paper's 'w/o Mix' ablation rather than the method, and every DEMO arm we ran before 2026-08-20 inherited that. It needs a dense NxN PPR matrix - build with analysis/scripts/make_ppr.py (photo 0.2GB, computers 0.8GB, cs 1.3GB, yelp 8.4GB in float32; ogbn-arxiv 115GB; ogbn-mag 2.2TB is not computable). Use --set mixup=false to run the ablation on purpose. energy_loss=True is DEMO's per-node second-order reweighting; measured on Photo it costs 6.5x the compute and changes nothing (METHODOLOGY section 4).
_comment_amazon: amazon inherits yelp's block verbatim except input_dim (25 vs 32): both are binary real-fraud graphs with dense neighbourhoods, and transferring an untuned config is a stronger claim than tuning a new dataset. sim_topk_frac is the exception - it helps yelp (+0.0263) and hurts photo (-0.0586), so it is chosen on VALIDATION ONLY from the two arms A_sim1/A_sim0, never on test.
_comment_tfinance: tfinance inherits yelp's block verbatim except input_dim (10): the third real-fraud graph, untuned by design like amazon. sim_topk_frac is decided on validation from the two arms A_sim1.0 / A_sim0.0 (analysis/tables/arm_selection.json).
